outline.description: This chapter sets the stage by discussing the rapid growth of Large Language Models (LLMs) and the associated computational, memory, and environmental costs. It introduces the limitations of traditional post-training quantization and motivates the need for natively 1-bit model architectures, leading to the concept of 1.58-bit LLMs.
subtopics: The Scaling Challenge in Large Language Models
Limitations of Post-Training Quantization
The Memory Bandwidth Bottleneck: DRAM to SRAM Transfer
The Emergence of 1-bit Model Architectures (BitNet)
From BitNet to BitNet b1.58: Introducing Ternary Weights {-1, 0, 1}
The Mathematical Significance of 1.58 Bits in the Binary System

outline.description: This chapter dives into the technical architecture of BitNet b1.58. It details the modifications made to the original BitNet, including the novel quantization functions for weights and activations, and the integration of LLaMA-like components to ensure compatibility with the open-source ecosystem.
subtopics: The BitNet Architecture: Replacing nn.Linear with BitLinear
Training from Scratch: 1.58-bit Weights and 8-bit Activations
Weight Quantization: The Absmean Quantization Function
The RoundClip Mechanism and Weight Scaling
Activation Quantization: Per-Token Scaling and Zero-Point Removal
LLaMA-alike Components: RMSNorm, SwiGLU, and Rotary Embedding
Modeling Capability: Feature Filtering through Explicit Zero Weights
Ecosystem Compatibility: Integration with Huggingface, vLLM, and llama.cpp

outline.description: This chapter comprehensively evaluates BitNet b1.58 against a full-precision (FP16) LLaMA baseline. It covers both the modeling performance (perplexity and zero-shot accuracy) and the hardware efficiency metrics (memory, latency, energy, and throughput) that make BitNet b1.58 a breakthrough architecture.
subtopics: Experimental Setup: RedPajama Dataset and FP16 LLaMA Baseline
Evaluating Perplexity on WikiText2 and C4 Datasets
Zero-Shot Performance on End Tasks (ARC, Hellaswag, Winogrande, PIQA, etc.)
GPU Memory and Latency Optimization Using 2-bit Kernels
Energy Consumption Analysis: FP16 Operations vs. INT8 Addition
Throughput Scaling: Batch Size and Sequence Length Comparisons on A100 GPUs
Scalability in Training Tokens: The 2T Tokens Experiment and Generalization

outline.chapter_title: The New Scaling Law and Pareto Improvements
outline.description: This chapter explains how BitNet b1.58 establishes a new scaling law that redefines the trade-off between model size and inference cost. It details the Pareto improvements demonstrated by 1.58-bit models over their 16-bit counterparts.
subtopics: Defining the New Scaling Law for 1.58-bit LLMs
Efficiency Equivalencies: 13B b1.58 vs. 3B FP16 LLM
Efficiency Equivalencies: 30B b1.58 vs. 7B FP16 LLM
Efficiency Equivalencies: 70B b1.58 vs. 13B FP16 LLM
Understanding Pareto Improvements in LLM Design

outline.description: This concluding chapter explores the broader implications of 1.58-bit LLMs on future AI research and deployment. It discusses how the unique properties of BitNet b1.58 can solve current challenges in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, long context handling, edge computing, and custom hardware design.
subtopics: 1-bit Mixture-of-Experts (MoE): Reducing Memory and Communication Overhead
Native Support for Long Sequences: Compressing KV Caches
Deploying LLMs on Edge and Mobile Devices
CPU-Friendly Execution for 1.58-bit Models
The Vision for 1-bit LLM Specific Hardware Optimizations
